claim_text: SAME-R aimed to link the sizes of liquid smoke droplets in low gravity to the conditions under which the smoke was generated and transported.
source_excerpt: the primary objective of the SAME-R investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity and to relate the droplet size distribution to the smoke generation and smoke transport conditions in the experiment.

claim_text: SAME-R completed 66 flight test points.
source_excerpt: SAME-R flight tests were conducted from July 16, to September 9, 2010, successfully completing 66 test points.

claim_text: The post-flight ground tests were intended to evaluate the lognormal distribution assumption used by the SAME and SAME-R moment method.
source_excerpt: After SAME-R flight tests, three major post–flight ground tests were performed to improve data reduction process and to validate the lognormal distribution assumption, the key to the moment method employed by SAME and SAME-R.

claim_text: For the reflight, SAME-R used M-pass in place of one commercial diagnostic enclosure described for SAME.
source_excerpt: a new instrument, M-pass, developed in-house GRC, was used to replace one of the two Commercial Diagnostic Enclosures that includes a DustTrak and an ionization detector used in SAME.

claim_text: SAME-R used a moment method that relies on a lognormal distribution assumption.
source_excerpt: the lognormal distribution assumption, the key to the moment method employed by SAME and SAME-R.

claim_text: SAME aimed to determine the size of liquid smoke particles in low gravity.
source_excerpt: One of the major goals of this investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity and to relate the droplet size distribution to the smoke generation and smoke transport conditions in the experiment.

claim_text: The SAME team hypothesized that liquid smoke droplets would be larger in microgravity than in otherwise comparable normal-gravity conditions.
source_excerpt: it is hypothesized that liquid aerosol smokes produced in microgravity will exhibit substantially larger droplet sizes than under the same conditions in normal gravity

claim_text: SPICE aimed to characterize laminar smoke points of nonbuoyant jet diffusion flames across different microgravity coflow conditions.
source_excerpt: Identify the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames under various co-flow conditions in microgravity.

claim_text: To locate the smoke point, SPICE varied the fuel flow rate and used the onset of soot emission as the criterion.
source_excerpt: Fuel flow rates were adjusted to identify the smoke point, marked by the flame's transition to emitting soot.

claim_text: The presentation reports flight smoke particle sizes from 100 to 600 nm.
source_excerpt: Particle sizes ranged from 100 to 600 nm

source_excerpt: The experimental results show that, for the materials tested, a substantial portion of the smoke particles are below 500 nm in diameter.

claim_text: Higher coflow velocity increased the smoke-point flame length in the microgravity tests.
source_excerpt: In microgravity conditions increasing the coflow velocity or decreasing the burner diameter increased the smoke point flame length.

claim_text: The SPICE extension reported smoke points for methane burning in air.
source_excerpt: Smoke points were found for methane, ethane, ethylene, and propane burning in air.

claim_text: The Fire Safety Journal paper reports 55 smoke points from ISS tests.
source_excerpt: Microgravity was obtained on board the International Space Station. A total of 55 smoke points were found for ethylene, propane, propylene, and propylene/nitrogen mixtures.

claim_text: ESA reported plans to study the sizes of particles emitted by spreading flames during a partial-gravity flight campaign.
source_excerpt: A future ESA partial gravity flight campaign will be the occasion to analyse, for the first time, the size of the particles emitted by spreading flames under these conditions
attribution_note: Described as future work in a 2021 article.

claim_text: Ground tests used a scanning mobility particle sizer as a reference for measuring smoke particle size distributions.
source_excerpt: The ground tests included a Scanning Mobility Particle Sizer Spectrometer (SMPS) reference instrument for measuring particle size distributions of the smoke produced from overheating five common spacecraft materials.

claim_text: Electron microscopy of returned samples identified both agglomerates and spherical particles in pyrolysis smoke.
source_excerpt: From electron microcopy of samples returned to earth, it was found that pyrolysis smoke can form an agglomerate shape as well as a spherical shape, which had previously been the assumed shape.

claim_text: The conference paper reports smoke-point measurements for nonbuoyant jet diffusion flames in coflow aboard the ISS.
source_excerpt: Laminar smoke points were measured in non-buoyant laminar jet diffusion flames in coflowing air aboard the International Space Station.

claim_text: The NTRS abstract reports that smoke particles produced in low gravity were typically twice the size of those produced in normal gravity, with differences across materials.
source_excerpt: The results varied between materials but the smoke particles produced in low gravity were typically twice the size of particles produced in normal gravity.
quantity: particle size relative to normal gravity

claim_text: The authors report that smoke particles became substantially larger as airflow decreased.
source_excerpt: Particle dimensions increase substantially as air flow was decreased.

claim_text: The authors suggest that measuring more than one moment of the particle size distribution may improve detection and false alarm rejection compared with measuring a single moment.
source_excerpt: Detection methods that can measure more than one moment of the size distribution may show more successful detection and false alarm rejection than single moment detectors.

claim_text: The investigation aimed to use simulations to determine how gravity affects the growth of particles in pyrolysis smoke.
source_excerpt: The objective of this investigation was to use numerical simulation to explore the influence of gravity on pyrolysis smoke growth from a fundamental perspective.

claim_text: DAFT and DAFT-2 aimed to test whether a modified P-Trak particle counter could measure aerosols accurately in microgravity.
source_excerpt: DAFT / DAFT-2 tests that a modified P-Trak particulate counter would be accurate in microgravity.

claim_text: The BASS-II record identifies combustion models for designing fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth as an application.
source_excerpt: BASS-II results contribute to the combustion computational models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth.

claim_text: The investigation identifies improvements to Earth combustion modeling and fire safety standards as a potential application.
source_excerpt: On Earth, these advancements could improve combustion modeling by deepening our understanding of coupled thermal, chemical, and flow processes, which betters fire safety standards.

claim_text: The record identifies more efficient combustion technologies on Earth as a potential application of improved flame models.
source_excerpt: Improved numerical models for flame behavior lead to more efficient combustion technologies on Earth.

claim_text: The Cool Flames Investigation record identifies combustion models for fuels in spark-ignition and diesel engines as an Earth application.
source_excerpt: The research will also help combustion chemists to develop new computational models to compute combustion performance in for many practical applications on earth, including an understanding of how cool flame reactivity determines octane and cetane number for fuels in spark ignition and diesel engines.
